To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the CRSS of FeNiCoCr high entropy alloy is 175 MPm and is in agreement with the atomistic-modified PN model, (ii) slip nucleates at a dislocation source at the surface of the crystal, (iii) the dislocation source is a Frank–Read source, (iv) the dislocations are 1/2〈1 1 1〉 and 1/6〈2 1 1
the CRSS in high entropy alloy FeNiCoCrMo was found to be 175 MPm and that the atomistic-modified PN formalism can accurately predict this value.

We have experimentally determined the critical resolved shear stress in single crystal Fe _{0.25} Ni _{0.25 } Co _{0.25  } Cr _{0.25 } Mn _{0.5}  high entropy alloy and have shown that this value is in excellent agreement (175 MPa vs. 178 MP ^{a} ) with that obtained from atomistic-modified PN modeling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of slip nucleated plasticity in a single crystal FeNi 0.25 Co 0.25 Cr 0.25 Mn 0.25 high entropy alloy (HEA).
the development of a new class of materials that have the potential to be used in applications that demand high mechanical strength, good ductility, and high resistance to corrosion.
the study of the slip behavior of high entropy alloy FeNiCoCr Mn.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the atomistic-modified Nabarro–Herring model is a very effective and accurate tool for the prediction of slip nucleation.
slip nucleation in FeNiCoCr alloy occurs in the same manner as in conventional face centered cubic metals.
slip nucleation in FeNiCoCrMo high entropy alloy is similar to that in conventional alloys.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that atomistic simulations can be used as a powerful tool for designing high entropy alloys with superior mechanical properties and for studying the fundamental mechanisms of plastic deformation in these alloys.
the CRSS of FeNiCoCrMo high entropy alloy is comparable to that of the conventional single phase alloys.
the high entropy FeNiCrCoMn single crystal is a promising candidate for future structural applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CRSS in high entropy alloys can be accurately predicted using atomistic modeling.
the CRSS is controlled primarily by the Peierls stress which depends on the shear strength and the magnitude of the Burgers vector.
the high entropy FeNiCrCoMn single crystals are prone to slip nucleation on {111} planes.
